subject: Information Theory
title: Genetic Drift and Noise
description: A quick win: understand Genetic Drift and Noise.

hook.text: In a population of 10, a beneficial mutation can vanish by chance. In millions, it almost certainly spreads.

buildup.text: Genetic drift is random fluctuation in gene frequencies—pure noise in the evolutionary channel.

discovery.text: Small populations are noisier. Drift overwhelms selection, and harmful mutations can fix by luck alone.

twist.text: Drift isn't always bad. It explores the fitness landscape randomly, sometimes finding paths selection would miss.

climax.text: Effective population size determines signal-to-noise ratio. Larger populations transmit more evolutionary information.

punchline.text: Small populations drift. Large populations select. Size controls the noise.

quiz.question: Why is genetic drift more impactful in small populations?
options: Random chance overwhelms the selective signal
